issue.title: test_fresh_heartbeat_is_not_reclaimed fails under the full parallel lane: a 0.2s stale window cannot survive holder starvation
issue.description:
`tests/test_suite_gate.py::test_fresh_heartbeat_is_not_reclaimed` failed once under
`just check`'s escalated parallel lane and passed five consecutive serial reruns on the
identical tree.

OBSERVED on 2026-08-18 while landing epic sase-qd (Projects-tab current project) in
workspace sase_15. The diff under test touched only
`src/sase/ace/tui/modals/projects_pane.py` and two ACE test modules -- nothing in
`tests/_suite_gate*.py` or the pytest gate machinery. `just check` escalated to a full
parallel run: `1 failed, 33845 passed, 13 skipped, 72 warnings in 452.92s`.

FAILURE: `tests/test_suite_gate.py:745` -- `AssertionError` (the run reports it
truncated as `Asse...`); the test wraps its acquire in
`pytest.raises(pytest.UsageError, match="heartbeat")`, so the failure is that the
competing acquire did NOT raise, i.e. the holder was reclaimed when the test asserts it
must not be.

NOT REPRODUCED SERIALLY: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:randomly -p no:xdist -q
tests/test_suite_gate.py::test_fresh_heartbeat_is_not_reclaimed` passed 5/5 on the same
tree (4.06s, then 2.57s / 2.43s / 2.48s / 2.46s).

LIKELY ROOT CAUSE (read from the test, not measured): the test spawns a subprocess that
holds a `WorkerTokenLease` and calls `record_lease_progress('session')` in a `time.sleep(0.02)`
loop, then asserts a competing
`_lease(tmp_path, budget=1, timeout=0.35, stale_timeout=0.2).acquire(...)` raises rather
than reclaiming. The negative assertion only holds while the holder's heartbeat stays
fresher than a 200 ms stale window. Under a ~33.8k-test `pytest -n <N> --dist=worksteal`
run the holder subprocess can be descheduled past 200 ms, its grant looks stale, the
waiter reclaims it, `acquire` succeeds, and no `UsageError` is raised. The 20 ms
heartbeat cadence leaves only a 10x margin against CPU starvation, which a saturated
host erases.

INTRODUCED BY: f7e6acbf6 "fix(tests): reclaim wedged suite-gate worker-token grants"
(closes sase-q2), the commit that added heartbeat-based reclamation and this test.

SUGGESTED FIX: make the negative assertion independent of wall-clock scheduling --
drive the staleness decision from an injected clock or an explicitly written heartbeat
timestamp rather than a real 0.2s window, or widen `stale_timeout` far enough that a
descheduled holder cannot cross it. Prefer that over baselining: this node guards a real
safety property (a live holder must never be reclaimed), so a baselined entry would hide
regressions in the reclaim rule itself.

VERIFY WITH: `just test-contention -- tests/test_suite_gate.py`, repeated, expecting
green; then a full `just check-full`.
